account:
Today I read my appointments and held morning office hours before coming to the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection. I have not found the miller; the neighbour also says they have not seen the miller this morning, so the inspection has not been completed. My remaining appointments include lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea with the neighbour at three, and office time from four-thirty. Builder requested a brief great-hall lighting inspection at six, and I asked the secretary to record it.

The unusual news is repeated, vague talk among townsfolk about a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Nobody I have spoken with has explained a concrete change. The neighbour explicitly says they have not witnessed one. Some townsfolk mention the baker, neighbour, and innkeeper in connection with these reports, and one said the innkeeper carried a sack of bread at the bakery. Those are reports, not things I personally saw.

The neighbour did give a specific firsthand account: Builder gave the baker a lantern and planks last night. I do not know their purpose. They could be supplies for some work or lighting at the bakery, but I have no basis for concluding that they are connected to a bridge or port change. Builder's hall-lighting appointment is another known activity involving lighting, though I do not know whether it is connected. I intend to ask the baker directly rather than pass the vague reports on as facts.
